newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government to examine possible VAT cut.
newsitem.headline: French government to examine possible VAT cut.

text.p: Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, presenting his new government's priorities to parliament, said he would launch an examination into a possible cut in Value Added Tax (VAT), or sales tax.
"To sustain growth, we need taxation which does more to favour consumption," Jospin told the National Assembly.
"I am asking the economy, finance and industry minister to examine the scope for a reduction in VAT."
He did not give a target figure for the tax, which currently stands at 20.6 percent.

Jospin also pledged to make good on the Socialists' promise to transfer payroll charges that fund health care gradually on to a widened CSG tax, which applies to most income including savings and retirement benefits.

"To promote employment and social justice, we must tax income from work less and eliminate the undeserved priviledges that other sorts of income enjoy. We will gradually transfer payroll charges that pay for health insurance on to a widened social levy that applies to all income including investment income," Jospin said.
